core_obligations: Use the adjunction to express the desired isomorphism as the counit tensored with the identity on M (proof lines 2673-2684).
Show this map is an isomorphism by the affine translation or by stalks (proof lines 2684-2692).
proof_roadmap: The isomorphism by algebra or stalks (proof lines 2684-2692).
difficulty_reason: For a pseudo-coherent closed immersion i : Z -> X, an object M of D_QCoh(O_X) locally of tor-amplitude in [a, infinity) and K in D^+_QCoh(O_X), the lemma asserts a canonical isomorphism RSheafHom(O_Z, K) otimes^L_{O_Z} Li^*M = RSheafHom(O_Z, K otimes^L_{O_X} M) in D(O_Z) (statement lines 2641-2671). The proof observes that a map from the left hand side to the right hand side is the same as a map Ri_*RSheafHom(O_Z, K) otimes^L_{O_X} M -> K otimes^L_{O_X} M, by Lemmas labelled lemma-sheaf-with-exact-support-adjoint and lemma-sheaf-with-exact-support-ext, and takes for this map the counit Ri_*RSheafHom(O_Z, K) -> K tensored with the identity on M (proof lines 2673-2684). To see that this map is an isomorphism under the hypotheses, one translates into algebra using Lemma labelled lemma-sheaf-with-exact-support-quasi-coherent and applies More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-internal-hom-evaluate-tensor-isomorphism part (3), with the alternative route of looking at stalks as in the second proof of Lemma labelled lemma-flat-bc-sheaf-with-exact-support (proof lines 2684-2692). Recognising the adjunction that converts the desired isomorphism into a map given by the counit, and then discharging the isomorphism by the affine translation or by stalks, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
